scope: C35 signed release verification and data-safe upgrades: detached Ed25519 attestations over an already packaged C31 artifact, verification against an independently supplied trusted key, and install/upgrade/rollback that never discard newer accepted data. Delivered scripts/verify-release.mjs, scripts/sign-release.mjs, scripts/install-release.mjs, tests/release/upgrade-recovery.mjs, tests/fixtures/miragemesh/C35/, docs/evidence/release-verification.json and the signed-release documentation in docs/release/ARTIFACTS.md and docs/release/USER_GUIDE.md. Verified on a real packaged artifact with ephemeral test keys: a changed artifact byte, a changed manifest byte, missing evidence, an untrusted or malformed key and an expired manifest all fail closed; a stale revision and a replayed downgrade cannot replace the accepted authority; install, upgrade and rollback leave the data directory byte-identical and refuse a store schema newer than the signed target. The source build remains the documented primary path with no release key.
source_identity_algorithm: scripts/source_identity.py: sorted tracked/untracked non-ignored paths excluding SHA256SUMS.txt and docs/evidence/, path NUL sha256(bytes), then sha256 of the concatenation; reproduced here without Python because the host has no Python interpreter
commit_note: No commit was created by the agent. The user pushed the implementation; this identity is recomputed after the CI regression fix and covers all C35 source, fixtures, tests, documentation and tooling edits before progress and handoff bookkeeping. The packaged artifact provenance records this same identity, proving the tested artifact was assembled from exactly this source tree. No ref, push, publication or hosted run was performed by the agent.

results.fixture_engine_note: Fixes the hosted web-foundation failure: on a matching linux-amd64 host the installer runs the real engine check, and the synthetic upgrade artifact previously shipped the real 0.0.1 engine while claiming 0.0.2, so the upgrade path failed with engine_check_failed and the two following rollback tests failed with no_previous_release.

observed_limitations: Host is windows/amd64 while the packaged artifact platform is linux-amd64. Install/upgrade/rollback file and data-safety semantics were exercised end to end, but the installed Linux engine --version check was skipped as foreign-platform. A native Linux run of the same suite remains unrecorded.

npm run build cannot complete natively on this Windows host: internal/storage uses Unix syscalls (syscall.Stat_t, O_NOFOLLOW, Flock), so build:engine exits 1 while preserving the previous binary. GOOS=linux go vet and GOOS=linux go build pass, and the packaged artifact used the existing linux-amd64 engine binary.

npm test on this host reports 125 tests, 98 pass, 26 fail, 1 skipped. Every failure is a host limitation, not a C35 regression: tests that spawn dist/engine/miragemesh receive ENOENT because the file is a Linux ELF, and tests asserting a native Go build fail on the Unix-only storage syscalls. The 11 C35 tests pass within that run.

scripts/validate_repo.py, scripts/plan.py validate and scripts/source_identity.py could not run because Python is absent; npm run validate:plan and the equivalent Node identity calculation passed. CI runs the Python checks on ubuntu-24.04.

rollback_or_recovery_observation: C35 changes no database schema, migration or data format. Its own rollback path was exercised: a recorded previous release is reactivated only after its installed bytes are re-verified, the data directory is untouched, and an upgrade can follow. Reverting the C35 source removes the signed-artifact path while leaving the C31 packaging and documented source build intact.
release_limits: No production release key, published fingerprint, published signature or published artifact is created here. Authorized publication and the clean-host installed full-workflow proof remain C40.
The attestation binds an artifact built from a dirty working tree; provenance reports dirty true and verification emits source_dirty. It is not a releasable publication.
The verified artifact contract is linux-amd64; other hosts are refused unless --allow-foreign-platform is given for staging, and such an install cannot run its engine check.
